videos.title: पहले यह जान लो: cell, शरीर और plant की ज़रूरी बातें
videos.goal: तुम cell के parts, chromosome sets, शरीर के अंदर की जगहों और plant positions को छोटे examples से समझोगे; आगे tissue की बनावट और काम जोड़ पाओगे।
prerequisites_taught: Cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus and basic plant-cell parts
Chromosome sets, DNA copying and nuclear versus cell division
Body covering, cavity, lumen and gland duct
Contraction, relaxation, fatigue and voluntary control
Root and shoot tips, nodes, internodes, leaf base and girth
Photosynthesis, food storage and root water–mineral uptake
videos.opening_hook: एक cell की बनावट देखकर उसके काम का अंदाज़ा कैसे लगाओगे?
videos.story_or_analogy: खाली tube से lumen और lining का फर्क; मुड़ती पट्टी और खिंचकर लौटते rubber band से flexibility और elasticity का फर्क दिखाएँगे। ये outside, standard textbook-level examples हैं।
videos.why_this_unit: ये सीधे chapter में लगने वाली outside foundations हैं। हर prerequisite को छोटी explanation और example से सिखाएँगे; इनके पीछे के अलग chapters नहीं खोलेंगे।

videos.title: Tissue क्या है? Cell से पूरे शरीर तक
videos.goal: तुम tissue की definition, division of labour, biological organisation और animal tissues का पूरा visual overview समझोगे।
videos.opening_hook: शरीर के सारे cells एक ही काम क्यों नहीं करते?
videos.story_or_analogy: काम बाँटकर चलती team से division of labour समझाएँगे; फिर book के cell–tissue–organ–organ system–organism क्रम पर लौटेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Definition और organisation के बाद animal-tissue tree पढ़ना अर्थपूर्ण होगा। Figure के सभी groups, labels और body locations को तय reading path से समझाएँगे।

videos.title: Epithelial tissue: layers, shapes और काम
videos.goal: तुम epithelial sheets, basement membrane, barrier और gland formation समझोगे; simple, stratified, pseudostratified, keratinised और transitional forms को figures में पहचानोगे।
videos.opening_hook: शरीर की हर lining एक जैसी होती, तो protection और exchange दोनों कैसे होते?
videos.story_or_analogy: पतली और कई layers वाली covering की तुलना केवल thickness और protection का संबंध समझाने के लिए करेंगे; epithelial details book से ही पढ़ेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: पहले sheet की पूरी बनावट, फिर layers और shape के आधार पर types पढ़ेंगे। हर type की location और function जोड़कर figures में labels, nuclei, cilia और cell arrangement पहचानेंगे।

videos.title: Connective tissue: matrix से support और heat बचाने तक
videos.goal: तुम matrix और fibres की भूमिका, connective-tissue types की locations और functions, उनके figures और subcutaneous fat वाले HPAS 2020 question की reasoning समझोगे।
videos.opening_hook: Blood और bone इतने अलग दिखते हैं, फिर दोनों connective tissue कैसे हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: Cells के बीच का material बदलने से पूरे tissue का काम कैसे बदलता है, यह book के blood, cartilage और bone examples को साथ रखकर दिखाएँगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Matrix की समझ से fibre properties और tissue differences निकलते हैं। इसके बाद blood cells, Haversian canals, canaliculi, chondrocytes और adipocytes की visual पहचान तथा heat-loss question समझ में आएगा।

videos.title: Muscle कैसे काम करती है? Skeletal और smooth muscle
videos.goal: तुम muscle contraction का book-level क्रम, muscle classes, skeletal muscle की movement और posture में भूमिका तथा smooth muscle और peristalsis समझोगे।
videos.opening_hook: हाथ तुम अपनी मर्ज़ी से चलाते हो, लेकिन खाना अंदर आगे कैसे बढ़ता है?
videos.story_or_analogy: Tube पर आगे बढ़ती दबाव की wave से peristalsis समझाएँगे; इसे केवल movement की analogy रखेंगे, microscopic mechanism नहीं।
videos.why_this_unit: Contraction के result और conditions से शुरू करके skeletal और smooth fibres की shape, nuclei, location और control को उनके काम से जोड़ेंगे।

videos.title: Cardiac muscle, attachment और neuron का signal
videos.goal: तुम cardiac muscle की बनावट और pumping, 3 muscle types के differences, cardiac statement question, muscle-to-bone attachment और neuron में signal का रास्ता समझोगे।
videos.opening_hook: Heart की muscle और हाथ की muscle में stripes हों, तो क्या दोनों का control भी एक जैसा होगा?
videos.why_this_unit: Cardiac structure के बाद तीनों muscle types को समान criteria पर compare करेंगे। Questions से control और attachment जाँचेंगे, फिर neuron के labelled path से impulse और synaptic transmission समझाएँगे। Tendon–ligament distinction और typical chemical synapse की explanation को outside clarification कहेंगे।

videos.title: Cell division और plant tissues का पूरा नक्शा
videos.goal: तुम mitosis–meiosis और plant–animal cytokinesis के differences समझोगे तथा plant-tissue classification के सभी groups को सही जगह रख पाओगे।
videos.opening_hook: Plant की बढ़ती tip और उसकी मजबूत पुरानी stem में cells का काम एक जैसा क्यों नहीं होता?
videos.why_this_unit: Plant growth से पहले division comparisons समझेंगे। Division count, daughter cells, ploidy, crossing over, cell plate और cleavage furrow के बाद दोनों plant-classification trees को basis, branches और examples सहित पढ़ेंगे। गलत DNA/chromosome generalisation को outside clarification से ठीक करेंगे।

videos.title: Meristems: plant कहाँ और कैसे बढ़ता है?
videos.goal: तुम meristematic cells की features और apical, lateral तथा intercalary meristems की positions को length और girth की growth से जोड़ोगे; location question हल करोगे।
videos.opening_hook: Plant की लंबाई और stem की मोटाई क्या एक ही जगह से बढ़ती हैं?
videos.why_this_unit: Active division करने वाले cells से शुरू करके plant figure पर tips, sides और intercalary positions पढ़ेंगे। Location–growth comparison के तुरंत बाद root tips only वाले distractor सहित practice करेंगे।

videos.title: Permanent tissues: storage, flexibility और strength
videos.goal: तुम differentiation, parenchyma की specialisations, collenchyma और sclerenchyma की बनावट, locations और functions समझोगे; comparison और जुड़े questions हल करोगे।
videos.opening_hook: एक plant में नरम हिस्सा, मुड़ने वाला stalk और कठोर husk—तीनों कैसे बनते हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: Book के leaf stalk, aquatic plant और coconut husk को साथ रखकर flexibility, buoyancy और strength के अलग tissue solutions दिखाएँगे।
videos.why_this_unit: Differentiation से simple permanent tissues तक एक पूरी chain बनती है। हर tissue की structure–function explanation के बाद 8-criterion comparison और climber, lignin तथा buoyancy questions करेंगे। Division और wall के absolute claims तथा ambiguous climber wording पर outside clarification अलग होगी।

videos.title: Xylem और phloem: transport के अलग काम
videos.goal: तुम complex tissues का basis, xylem और phloem के components, उनके अलग roles, labelled anatomy, cambium और transport arrows समझोगे; exceptions के साथ comparison करोगे।
videos.opening_hook: Plant में water और food दोनों चलते हैं, तो transport tissue एक ही तरह का क्यों नहीं है?
videos.why_this_unit: Classification के बाद प्रत्येक component का conduction, storage या support वाला काम समझेंगे। Figures में pits, sieve plates, cambium और arrows पढ़कर comparison करेंगे; living/dead cells, wall chemistry और support पर गलत absolute rules नहीं बनाएँगे। अंत में xylem से excluded component का question करेंगे।

videos.title: Plant की बाहरी covering और gas exchange
videos.goal: तुम epidermis और cuticle का protective role तथा stomata और guard cells का फर्क समझकर दोनों practice questions हल करोगे।
videos.opening_hook: Leaf की covering protection भी दे और gases को आने-जाने भी दे—यह कैसे होगा?
videos.why_this_unit: दोनों questions plant surface के जुड़े काम पूछते हैं। Surface से pore तक labelled reading करेंगे; epidermis–cuticle और stomatal pore–guard cell distinctions को ज़रूरी outside clarification के रूप में समझाएँगे, unclear thickest wording को universal rule नहीं बनाएँगे।

plan.chapter_flow: पहले 7 minutes में सीधे ज़रूरी prerequisites examples के साथ सिखाएँगे। फिर tissue और organisation से animal-tissue overview बनाएँगे; epithelial, connective, muscle और nervous tissue को structure, location और function से जोड़ेंगे। इसके बाद division और plant-classification trees से meristems, differentiation, simple permanent tissues और complex transport tissues तक बढ़ेंगे। अंत में protective surface और gas-exchange questions समझेंगे। हर content type अपना teaching pattern रखेगा; figures के labels और tables के criteria पूरे पढ़ेंगे। Practice questions संबंधित explanation के बाद आएँगे और outside clarifications साफ़ अलग रहेंगी। Topic narration 99 minutes और prerequisite सहित कुल 106 minutes है।

videos.title: पहले यह जान लो: cell, शरीर और plant की ज़रूरी बातें

frame.process: Identify basic cell compartments and plant-cell parts.
frame.how: Move from the cell boundary inward and connect each part with its role.
frame.when: Before interpreting tissue-cell structure.
frame.conditions: Plant-cell parts vary; not every plant cell contains chloroplasts.
frame.atmosphere: A simple cell diagram beside a familiar room.

frame.process: Distinguish chromosome sets, DNA copying and the division of nucleus and cell.
frame.how: Use paired instruction books to separate set number from copying.
frame.when: DNA copying precedes the divisions being introduced; nuclear and cytoplasmic division are distinguished.
frame.conditions: Use a typical diploid body cell and haploid gamete as introductory examples.
frame.atmosphere: A cell diagram with paired books and chromosome copies.

frame.process: Locate coverings, cavities, lumens, linings and ducts.
frame.how: Read a hollow tube from its open space through its wall.
frame.when: Before epithelial layers and glands.
frame.conditions: Distinguish an organ's internal passage from its lining and underlying tissue.
frame.atmosphere: A cut-open tube beside a simplified hollow organ.

frame.process: Distinguish diffusion, absorption and secretion.
frame.how: Compare movement down a concentration difference with uptake and cellular release.
frame.when: During exchange, nutrient uptake and gland activity.
frame.conditions: Diffusion requires a concentration difference and a path permitting movement.
frame.atmosphere: Perfume spreading, intestinal uptake and a saliva-producing gland.

frame.process: Distinguish strength, flexibility, elasticity and rigidity.
frame.how: Compare resistance to pulling, bending, recovery and stiffness.
frame.when: When interpreting the mechanical roles of tissues.
frame.conditions: The properties are distinct and may coexist in a material.
frame.atmosphere: Rope, a bendable strip, a rubber band and a stiff ruler.

frame.process: Explain contraction, relaxation, fatigue and voluntary control.
frame.how: Connect force generation and reduced tension to simple body movements.
frame.when: During activity, release and repeated effort.
frame.conditions: Contraction need not shorten a muscle; conscious control differs across muscle actions.
frame.atmosphere: Lifting and holding a book, then lowering the arm.

frame.process: Locate plant tips, nodes, internodes, leaf bases and girth.
frame.how: Trace a seedling from root tip upward and compare length with thickness.
frame.when: Before locating growth tissues.
frame.conditions: Positions are defined relative to plant organs, not simply height above ground.
frame.atmosphere: A whole seedling with a magnified stem segment.

frame.process: Separate food production, food storage and water–mineral uptake.
frame.how: Follow inputs into a leaf and distinguish production from storage and root uptake.
frame.when: Photosynthesis occurs under suitable light conditions; stored food can be used later.
frame.conditions: Photosynthesis needs light, chlorophyll, carbon dioxide and water.
frame.atmosphere: A plant in sunlight with leaves, roots and a food-storing potato.

beats.say: Cell को छोटे कमरे की तरह सोचो, लेकिन यह living unit है। Cell membrane उसकी boundary है और चीज़ों के अंदर-बाहर जाने को control करती है। अंदर cytoplasm होता है, जहाँ कई cell activities चलती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Room analogy beside a cell; label cell membrane and cytoplasm.

beats.say: Nucleus में DNA होता है, जिसमें cell के काम के instructions रहते हैं। Plant cell में membrane के बाहर cell wall भी होती है, जो support देती है। Wall और membrane को एक ही चीज़ मत समझना।
beats.on_screen: Outside-to-inside labels: cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus; DNA inside nucleus.

beats.say: Vacuole को storage space की तरह समझो; इसमें पानी और उसमें घुली चीज़ें रह सकती हैं। बड़े vacuole का पानी plant cell को तना हुआ रखने में भी मदद करता है। Chloroplast में photosynthesis होता है, लेकिन हर plant cell में chloroplast नहीं होता; आम root cells इसका example हैं।
beats.on_screen: Plant cell with large vacuole and chloroplasts; contrast with a typical root cell.

beats.say: अब DNA को instruction book समझो। DNA, proteins के साथ मिलकर chromosomes बनाता है। Chromosome set का मतलब हर तरह के chromosome की 1 पूरी collection है; diploid में 2 sets और haploid में 1 set होता है।
beats.on_screen: One complete colour-coded chromosome collection = haploid; two matching collections = diploid.

beats.say: आम body cells को somatic cells कहते हैं; ये सामान्य तौर पर diploid होते हैं। Reproduction में काम आने वाले sperm और egg जैसे gametes haploid होते हैं। Gametes बनाने वाली शुरुआती cells और तैयार gametes को एक जैसा मत मानना।
beats.on_screen: Typical somatic cell: 2 sets; sperm and egg: 1 set each; precursor distinguished from gamete.

beats.say: अब खाली pipe देखो। बीच का खाली रास्ता lumen है; उसे घेरे हुए अंदर की layer lining है। Intestine जैसे hollow organ में भी अंदर का रास्ता और उसकी lining अलग चीज़ें हैं।
beats.on_screen: Cut-open pipe beside intestine cross-section; lumen and lining highlighted separately.

beats.say: Body covering बाहर ढकती है, जैसे skin; cavity शरीर के अंदर की जगह है। Lining के नीचे supporting tissue होता है, lumen नहीं। Gland duct वह passage है जो gland की बनाई चीज़ आगे पहुँचाता है, जैसे saliva को mouth तक लाने वाला duct।
beats.on_screen: Body covering and cavity; enlarged lumen → lining → underlying tissue; gland → duct → mouth.

beats.say: Perfume की smell पास से दूर तक कैसे पहुँचती है? Diffusion में particles का net movement ज़्यादा concentration से कम concentration की ओर होता है। Concentration का मतलब किसी जगह की तय मात्रा में particles कितने हैं; रास्ता ऐसा होना चाहिए जिससे वे जा सकें।
beats.on_screen: Perfume particles spreading; high → low concentration with net-movement arrow.

beats.say: Absorption में कोई चीज़ अंदर ली जाती है, जैसे intestine से nutrients शरीर में जाना। Secretion में cell कोई चीज़ बनाकर बाहर छोड़ता है, जैसे gland से saliva निकलना। Diffusion movement का तरीका बताता है; absorption और secretion में ध्यान अंदर लेने और बाहर छोड़ने पर है।
beats.on_screen: Three distinct panels: diffusion, nutrient absorption, saliva secretion.

beats.say: रस्सी खींचने पर आसानी से न टूटे, तो उसमें pulling force सहने की strength है। कोई strip आसानी से मुड़ जाए, तो वह flexible है। इसलिए strong होने का मतलब हमेशा कड़ा होना नहीं है; रस्सी strong भी हो सकती है और flexible भी।
beats.on_screen: Rope resisting pull, then bending; strength ≠ rigidity.

beats.say: Rubber band को सीमा के अंदर खींचकर छोड़ो, वह पुरानी shape में लौटता है: यह elasticity है। केवल मुड़ जाना flexibility है; वापस लौटना उसका ज़रूरी हिस्सा नहीं। Rigidity shape बदलने का विरोध है, जैसे stiff ruler का आसानी से न मुड़ना।
beats.on_screen: Bendable strip; rubber band stretching and recovering; stiff ruler resisting bending.

beats.say: किताब उठाते समय muscle force बनाती है: इसे contraction कहते हैं। Contraction में muscle छोटी हो सकती है, लेकिन किताब स्थिर पकड़े रहने पर भी force बनता है। इसलिए contraction का मतलब केवल छोटा होना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Arm lifting a book, then holding it still; force indicated in both.

beats.say: Relaxation में muscle का active tension घटता है। बार-बार काम करने पर force बनाए रखने की क्षमता घटे, तो वह fatigue है। अपनी इच्छा से हाथ उठाना voluntary control है; heartbeat को हर बार तुम्हारे आदेश की ज़रूरत नहीं, इसलिए वह involuntary है।

beats.say: एक छोटे plant में root का सबसे आगे वाला सिरा root tip है। Shoot tip ऊपर बढ़ते shoot का सिरा है। इन्हें केवल नीचे और ऊपर मत याद करना; tip का मतलब उस root या shoot का अपना end है।

beats.say: Stem पर जहाँ leaf जुड़ती है, वह node है। लगातार 2 nodes के बीच का stem, internode है; किसी छोटी branch पर 2 leaves के जुड़ने की जगह और बीच का हिस्सा देखो। Leaf base, leaf का वह हिस्सा है जिससे वह stem से जुड़ती है।

frame.process: Cells form a functional group called a tissue.
frame.how: Read the definition through cells, grouping and shared function.
frame.when: Introduce before tissue categories and organisation.
frame.conditions: A shared function is essential; an arbitrary collection is insufficient.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a group of muscle cells working together.

frame.process: Distinguish plant tissues from animal tissues.
frame.how: Classify by whether the constituent cells are plant or animal cells.
frame.when: After defining tissue and before explaining shared work.
frame.conditions: Combining means organised grouping, not necessarily cell fusion.
frame.atmosphere: Compare a plant and an animal as sources of their respective tissues.

frame.process: Tissue organisation distributes the organism's work.
frame.how: Shared work reduces the wider workload placed on individual cells.
frame.when: Explain after grouping cells and before introducing the hierarchy.

videos.title: Epithelial tissue: layers, shapes और काम

frame.process: Epithelium covers organs and lines cavities as a continuous cellular sheet.
frame.how: Closely packed cells have little intervening material; an extracellular fibrous basement membrane usually separates them from underlying tissue.
frame.when: Read from the exposed surface through the epithelial sheet to the basement membrane and underlying tissue.
frame.conditions: Intercellular spaces are almost absent; retain the source's qualification 'usually' for basement-membrane separation.
frame.atmosphere: A sectional view of a body lining, with the exposed side above and supporting tissue below.

frame.process: An epithelial barrier helps keep body systems separate.
frame.how: Close cellular association restricts uncontrolled passage while particular epithelial types permit transport.
frame.when: The barrier operates while the sheet remains intact; it is not a developmental sequence.
frame.conditions: Barrier does not mean that diffusion, absorption and secretion are universally prevented.
frame.atmosphere: Two neighbouring body compartments separated by a continuous epithelial sheet.

frame.process: Epithelial cells specialise for secretion, and inward folding can form a multicellular gland.
frame.how: Secretory specialisation adds a function; a portion of the epithelial sheet sometimes folds inward.
frame.when: Explain secretory specialisation, inward folding and the resulting gland in that order; no age or fixed timing is given.
frame.conditions: The source says 'often' for specialisation and 'sometimes' for inward folding, not that every epithelium forms a gland.
frame.atmosphere: A body lining shown in section, followed into an inward epithelial fold.

frame.process: Simple epithelial forms provide diffusion, absorption, secretion, protection and directed surface movement.
frame.how: One layer contains flat, short cuboidal or tall columnar cells; microvilli and cilia add different capabilities.
frame.when: Inspect layer number, cell shape, specialisations, locations and functions.
frame.conditions: Microvilli and cilia are not interchangeable; the listed columnar locations are broad associations rather than universal descriptions.
frame.atmosphere: Sections through exchange surfaces, kidney tubules, gland ducts and digestive or respiratory linings.

frame.process: Stratified epithelial linings protect exposed surfaces and gland ducts, with secretion in the columnar entry.
frame.how: Several layers are arranged beneath squamous, cuboidal or columnar surface cells.
frame.when: Read each tissue from its surface towards deeper cells; explain squamous renewal as older cells move upwards and are shed.
frame.conditions: Surface-cell shape determines the stratified name; deeper cells may have different shapes.
frame.atmosphere: Layered linings of the mouth, vagina, gland ducts and male urethra.

frame.process: Three epithelial specialisations emphasise apparent layering, a keratinised protective surface or stretch accommodation.
frame.how: Compare unequal cell heights, superficial keratinisation and stretch-dependent changes in a stratified lining.
frame.when: For transitional tissue, compare unstretched and stretched states as liquid volume changes.
frame.conditions: Pseudostratification is not true multilayering; keratinisation concerns superficial epithelial cells; urethral lining varies by region.
frame.atmosphere: Side-by-side respiratory, keratinised-surface and urinary-lining examples.

frame.process: The two figures distinguish epithelial forms through visible structural features.
frame.how: Read layer number, surface-cell shape, projections and nuclear levels along a fixed path.
frame.when: Read the four-form figure top to bottom, then the seven-form figure across its upper and lower groups and finally the right-hand block.
frame.conditions: These are comparative schematics, not a transformation sequence; apparent nuclear levels alone do not establish actual layering.
frame.atmosphere: Labelled epithelial blocks with an exposed surface above their supporting base.

beats.say: Epithelium ज़्यादातर organs को cover करता है और body cavities को line करता है। Covering किसी structure के ऊपर की sheet है; lining अंदर के खाली हिस्से के किनारे की sheet।

beats.say: अब exposed side से नीचे देखो। Epithelial cells tightly packed हैं और continuous sheet बनाती हैं। Cells के बीच cementing material बहुत कम है, और intercellular spaces, यानी cells के बीच के खाली हिस्से, लगभग नहीं हैं।

beats.say: Sheet के नीचे basement membrane देखो। Book के अनुसार यह extracellular fibrous membrane है, जो epithelium को नीचे के tissue से usually अलग करती है। Extracellular मतलब cells के बाहर; इसे किसी एक cell की plasma membrane मत समझना।

beats.say: इस sheet का एक नतीजा है separation: अलग body systems अलग बने रहते हैं। Epithelium उनके बीच barrier का काम करता है।

beats.say: Book का उदाहरण urinary lining है: tight junctions cells के बीच रास्ते seal करके toxic substances के reabsorption को रोकने में मदद करते हैं।

beats.say: अब इसी epithelium से gland बन सकती है। Epithelial cells अक्सर gland cells की extra specialisation लेती हैं, जो epithelial surface पर substances secrete कर सकती हैं।

beats.say: Simple epithelial types में 1 cell layer होती है। Squamous, cuboidal और columnar उनकी cell shapes बताते हैं।

beats.say: Simple squamous में flat cells की 1 layer है, और उनकी boundaries irregular हैं। Simple Cuboidal Epithelium को book short cylindrical cells की single layer कहती है; figure में cells cube-like हैं, लगभग जितनी ऊँची उतनी चौड़ी।

beats.say: Cuboidal cells में microvilli हो सकती हैं, जैसे proximal convoluted tubules में। Simple Columnar Epithelium में tall, slender cells की 1 layer होती है, जिसे book often ciliated बताती है। Microvilli और cilia को एक मत समझना।

beats.say: Simple squamous blood vessels और capillaries की lining, lungs के air sacs और kidney की Bowman’s capsule में मिलता है। इसका काम diffusion से transport है, जहाँ minimal protection चाहिए। पतली layer crossing distance कम रखती है, इसलिए exchange के लिए ठीक है।

beats.say: Simple cuboidal kidney की tubular lining और glandular ducts में है; काम absorption और secretion। Microvilli absorption के लिए available area बढ़ाती हैं। Cilia का काम अलग है: वे beat करके material को lining के साथ आगे चलाती हैं।

beats.say: Simple columnar के लिए table digestive tract और upper respiratory tract lining देती है; काम protection, absorption, mucus secretion और एक तय direction में movement हैं। Mucus lining को चिकना रखता है और particles पकड़ सकता है, जिससे नुकसान पहुँचाने वाला material सीधे cells से कम टकराता है। Cilia मिलकर beat करें, तो ऊपर का material आगे बढ़ता है। यानी mucus का बनना और उसका आगे चलना अलग काम हैं, जो मिलकर protection में मदद कर सकते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Show mucus lubricating the lining and trapping particles, followed by coordinated ciliary transport.

frame.process: Connective tissue connects, supports and packs body structures.
frame.how: Binding and supporting material maintains relationships between tissues and organs.
frame.when: Support is ongoing and particularly relevant during body movement.
frame.conditions: These are qualitative functional statements; no numerical scale or formula is supplied.
frame.atmosphere: Picture organs remaining supported as the body moves.

frame.process: Cells occupy an extracellular framework with ground substance and fibres.
frame.how: Read from surrounding matrix to embedded cells and then the three fibre types.
frame.when: This is a spatial arrangement, not a timed sequence; elastic recoil follows removal of force.
frame.conditions: Matrix consistency and fibre composition vary among tissues.
frame.atmosphere: A magnified connective-tissue field with separated cells and surrounding material.

frame.process: Secreted protein fibres give connective tissue mechanical properties.
frame.how: Collagen resists tension while elastic fibres stretch and recoil.
frame.when: Properties become evident during pulling, bending and release of force.
frame.conditions: Flexibility, strength and elasticity are distinct; deficient fibres compromise their respective contributions.
frame.atmosphere: Compare a tissue under force with the same tissue after release.

frame.process: The illustration locates cells, fibres, ground substance and a vessel.
frame.how: Follow leaders from upper left through the framework to lower-right cells and the matrix key.
frame.when: Read labels spatially; the leaders do not depict a sequence.
frame.conditions: Colours and line thickness distinguish illustrated components.
frame.atmosphere: A schematic tissue field, not a literal natural-colour view.

frame.process: Compare connective-tissue types by location and function.
frame.how: Contrast loose, dense and elastic tissues, then cartilage, bone, blood and adipose.
frame.when: Support is ongoing; elasticity matters during deformation and heat conservation during heat transfer.
frame.conditions: Different matrices and cellular specialisations suit different roles.
frame.atmosphere: A body-location comparison table linked to familiar tissues.

frame.process: Identify five connective-tissue panels and their labelled components.
frame.how: Read panels a to e, distinguishing cells, cell contents, fibres, matrix and canals.
frame.when: The panel order is a reading path, not a developmental sequence.
frame.conditions: Use the caption to separate crowded labels; do not assign the ambiguous red-cell label to a panel.
frame.atmosphere: A composite labelled figure of blood, bone, cartilage, areolar and adipose tissues.

frame.process: Select heat-loss prevention as the function tested for subcutaneous fat.
frame.how: Connect poor heat conduction with slower heat transfer and eliminate the distractors.
frame.when: Heat tends to move from warmer tissues toward cooler surroundings.
frame.conditions: Insulation slows heat loss rather than stopping it completely.
frame.atmosphere: An HPAS 2020 multiple-choice question after the adipose explanation.

videos.title: Muscle कैसे काम करती है? Skeletal और smooth muscle

frame.process: Muscle tissue consists of elongated cells containing contractile proteins.
frame.how: Read from tissue to fibre and then to proteins inside the fibre.
frame.when: Establish the cellular structure before explaining activity.
frame.conditions: Muscle fibre means a cell in this context.
frame.atmosphere: A tissue-to-cell schematic.

frame.process: Muscle generates active tension and subsequently relaxes.
frame.how: Activation enables contractile action; declining activation reduces active tension.
frame.when: Contraction precedes relaxation in the simplified teaching sequence.
frame.conditions: Force generation needs activation and energy; shortening is not obligatory.
frame.atmosphere: A deliberately moved limb.

frame.process: Muscle tissue is organised into three classes.
frame.how: Distinguish classes using location, cellular appearance and control.
frame.when: Introduce the tree before studying skeletal and smooth muscle.
frame.conditions: Traits of one class must not be generalised to all muscle.
frame.atmosphere: A three-branch classification tree.

frame.process: Skeletal muscle links cellular structure with attachment to bones.
frame.how: Move from bone association to fibre outline, bands and nuclei.
frame.when: Inspect structure before function.
frame.conditions: Multiple nuclei belong to a single cell; neighbouring fibres are not branches.
frame.atmosphere: An arm beside an enlarged skeletal fibre.

frame.process: The book characterises skeletal muscle as easily fatigued.
frame.how: Explain fatigue through declining ability to sustain force.
frame.when: During continued activity.
frame.conditions: Fatigue varies with muscle and activity; the book supplies no measurements.
frame.atmosphere: A familiar sustained muscle effort.

frame.process: Skeletal muscle produces movement and maintains posture.
frame.how: Muscle force either changes position or balances forces to preserve position.
frame.when: During movement and while holding a posture.
frame.conditions: Contraction need not produce visible shortening or motion.
frame.atmosphere: A moving arm followed by a supported body position.

frame.process: Alternative names describe skeletal association, banding and conscious control.
frame.how: Connect each name to its identifying property.
frame.when: After learning skeletal structure and function.
frame.conditions: Voluntary does not mean every contraction is consciously chosen.
frame.atmosphere: A student choosing to move a hand.

frame.process: The figure links skeletal fibres with an arm muscle.
frame.how: Read the left fibre group and label, then the bent arm at right.
frame.when: After the skeletal-muscle explanation.
frame.conditions: Colours are schematic; the image is not a process sequence.
frame.atmosphere: The described two-part Skeletal Muscle illustration.

frame.process: Smooth muscle has tapered unbranched cells with one central nucleus and no striations.
frame.how: Locate the tissue, inspect cell outline, then inspect its interior.
frame.when: Introduce smooth structure before peristalsis.
frame.conditions: Absence of bands does not imply absence of contractile proteins.
frame.atmosphere: Smooth cells associated with stomach, intestine, eye and blood vessels.

frame.process: The book describes smooth muscle as not fatiguing.
frame.how: Interpret this as suitability for sustained normal activity.
frame.when: During sustained organ activity.
frame.conditions: This is a broad fatigue-resistance statement, not unlimited performance.
frame.atmosphere: Repeated activity in internal organs.

frame.process: Peristalsis moves contents through a hollow organ.
frame.how: A travelling pattern of contraction behind and relaxation ahead propels contents.
frame.when: As digestive contents pass through the tract.
frame.conditions: Contractions must be coordinated rather than isolated squeezes.
frame.atmosphere: Food within an intestinal tube.

frame.process: Smooth muscle is also called visceral, Unstriated and Involuntary.
frame.how: Separate naming by location, appearance and control.
frame.when: After smooth structure and activity are understood.
frame.conditions: Appearance and voluntary control are independent criteria.
frame.atmosphere: A naming tree with separate criteria.

frame.process: The figure associates smooth cells with the intestine.
frame.how: Read cells and label at left, then the digestive illustration at right.
frame.when: After explaining smooth muscle and peristalsis.
frame.conditions: The side-by-side views show association, not stages of peristalsis.
frame.atmosphere: The described boxed Smooth Muscle illustration.

videos.title: Cardiac muscle, muscle का attachment और neuron का signal

frame.process: Cardiac muscle forms the contracting and relaxing heart wall.
frame.how: Read cylindrical, branched, striated fibres and their individual nuclei, then connect their collective action to pumping.
frame.when: Contraction and relaxation repeat during heart activity.
frame.conditions: The book gives the usual one-nucleus description for each fibre.
frame.atmosphere: A microscopic tissue view placed within the wall of a working heart.

frame.process: Cardiac muscle sustains repeated activity without ordinary fatigue.
frame.how: Explain the listed characteristic and its physiological limit.
frame.when: Across repeated contraction–relaxation cycles.
frame.conditions: Normal activity requires adequate oxygen and nutrient supply.
frame.atmosphere: A normally functioning heart; no experimental fatigue data are supplied.

frame.process: Cardiac activity helps pump and distribute blood.
frame.how: Heart-wall contraction generates pressure; relaxation permits renewed filling.
frame.when: Repeatedly, with filling between pumping actions.
frame.conditions: Inadequate pumping can leave tissues insufficiently supplied.
frame.atmosphere: The heart moving blood through the body's circulation.

frame.process: Classify cardiac muscle independently by appearance and control.
frame.how: Place it under striated appearance and involuntary control.
frame.when: Use both criteria whenever identifying a muscle type.
frame.conditions: Striations do not imply voluntary control.
frame.atmosphere: A two-criterion muscle classification.

frame.process: The illustration associates branching cardiac tissue with the heart.
frame.how: Read tissue, bands, nuclei, printed label and neighbouring heart.
frame.when: After learning the tissue features.
frame.conditions: The schematic network must not be mistaken for one multinucleated cell.
frame.atmosphere: The boxed cardiac-tissue and heart illustration.

frame.process: Compare skeletal, cardiac and visceral muscle.
frame.how: Compare location, function, appearance and control across all three.
frame.when: After the individual muscle types have been taught.
frame.conditions: Identification requires a combination of criteria.
frame.atmosphere: The book's three-row muscle comparison table.

frame.process: Recognise the three muscle illustrations.
frame.how: Inspect shape, bands, branching and nuclei in a fixed sequence.
frame.when: After comparing the table rows.
frame.conditions: Visible morphology supports identification but does not itself demonstrate conscious control.
frame.atmosphere: The skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle drawings beside the table.

frame.process: Test the statement that cardiac fibres are striated.
frame.how: Locate bands on fibres in the heart wall and connect them to organised contractile structures.
frame.when: Before selecting the incorrect statement.
frame.conditions: Striation is an appearance feature, not a control category.
frame.atmosphere: A brief microscopic recall within the practice question.

frame.process: Test whether cardiac muscle is voluntary.
frame.how: Classify control and contrast cardiac with skeletal muscle.
frame.when: While checking statement 2.
frame.conditions: Heartbeat does not require a conscious command for each contraction.
frame.atmosphere: An exam statement containing a misleading control category.

frame.process: Test the claim that cardiac tissue shares features with skeletal and visceral tissue.
frame.how: Compare striation and control separately.
frame.when: While checking statement 3.
frame.conditions: Shared features do not make cardiac tissue a mixture of two tissues.
frame.atmosphere: A compact three-type comparison for an exam question.

frame.process: Select the incorrect cardiac statement.
frame.how: Check all three statements and map the result to the supplied options.
frame.when: After the statement-level concept checks.
frame.conditions: The stem asks for the incorrect statement.
frame.atmosphere: The combined page-13 stem and page-14 answer options.

frame.process: Identify the muscle-to-bone attachment.
frame.how: Choose tendon and distinguish ligament, cartilage and None.
frame.when: When muscle contraction transmits a pull to bone.
frame.conditions: Muscle-to-bone and bone-to-bone connections must not be confused.
frame.atmosphere: A skeletal attachment shown beside the multiple-choice question.

frame.process: Read the pathway of communication between successive neurons.
frame.how: Trace the incoming axon, first synapse, receiving neuron, outgoing axon, terminal region and next neuron.
frame.when: Follow the illustrated signal direction from lower left to upper right.
frame.conditions: Axonal conduction and communication between separate cells are distinct.
frame.atmosphere: The labelled two-neuron diagram with blue directional arrows and circled synapses.

frame.process: Answer how neurons send messages to other cells.
frame.how: Explain electrical travel along the axon and transfer at a synapse.
frame.when: An impulse reaching the terminal can initiate chemical signalling to the next cell.
frame.conditions: At a typical chemical synapse the cells remain separated by a small gap.
frame.atmosphere: The same neuron diagram used to answer its introductory question.

videos.title: Cell division और plant tissues का पूरा नक्शा

frame.process: Compare mitosis and meiosis as chromosome-distribution mechanisms.
frame.how: Compare cell context, divisions, products, phases, chromosome sets and crossing over; correct the replication row.
frame.when: DNA replication precedes mitosis or meiosis I; meiosis has two successive divisions without another replication.
frame.conditions: The printed diploid outcome assumes a diploid starting cell; reproductive outcomes vary with life cycle.
frame.atmosphere: Two parallel division diagrams beside the supplied comparison table.

frame.process: Compare typical plant and animal mitosis and cytoplasmic partitioning.
frame.how: Contrast centrioles, asters, cell plate, cleavage furrow and sites of division.
frame.when: Discuss nuclear division before distinguishing the accompanying cytoplasmic partition.
frame.conditions: A rigid plant cell wall prevents animal-style pinching; the table describes typical higher-plant and animal cells.
frame.atmosphere: A walled plant cell and an animal cell dividing side by side.

frame.process: Classify plant tissues and locate each subtype or component at its correct level.
frame.how: Divide by active division, cellular composition and then subtype or component relationships.
frame.when: Read top down; arrows express membership rather than a temporal sequence.
frame.conditions: Permanent cells are generally differentiated and not actively dividing; visible cropped lists are not exhaustive.
frame.atmosphere: One combined tree with a plant outline and small identifying cell sketches.

beats.say: Book mitosis को somatic cells, यानी body cells से, और meiosis को germ cells से जोड़ती है। Products के काम में mitosis से somatic organs बनते हैं; meiosis को gamete formation से जोड़ा गया है। इसे शुरुआती तुलना समझो, हर life cycle का पूरा नियम नहीं।

beats.say: Mitosis में nucleus 1 बार divide होता है और आम तौर पर 2 daughter cells बनते हैं। Meiosis में 2 nuclear divisions, meiosis I और meiosis II, से आम तौर पर 4 products बनते हैं। यानी इस तुलना में meiotic products की गिनती दोगुनी है।
beats.on_screen: Mitosis: 1 → 2; meiosis: 1 → 2 → 4.

beats.say: Book mitotic daughters को diploid और meiotic daughters को haploid कहती है। Diploid में 2 chromosome sets, यानी 2n; haploid में 1 set, यानी n होता है। Mitosis में starting chromosome number बचता है, meiosis में आधा रह जाता है।
beats.on_screen: Diploid starting cell: mitosis 2n → 2n; meiosis 2n → n.

beats.say: Frequency में book mitosis को more frequent और meiosis को less frequent बताती है। कोई rate या numerical difference नहीं दिया है। Phases में mitosis का prophase, metaphase, anaphase और telophase 1-1 बार आता है; meiosis में हर phase 2 बार, और prophase I के 5 sub-phases हैं।
beats.on_screen: Qualitative frequency contrast; one phase sequence versus I and II; prophase I: 5 subdivisions.

beats.say: Crossing over को table mitosis में absent और meiosis में present दिखाती है। इसमें paired homologous chromosomes की non-sister chromatids के बीच corresponding DNA segments exchange होते हैं। यह meiosis के prophase I की घटना है, जिससे नए allele combinations बन सकते हैं।

beats.say: इन differences की वजह separation का तरीका है। Meiosis I में homologous partners अलग होते हैं, इसलिए sets आधे होते हैं; meiosis II में sister chromatids अलग होती हैं। Mitosis starting ploidy बचाता है, इसलिए diploid parent से diploid, लेकिन haploid parent से haploid daughters भी बन सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Homologues separate in I; sister chromatids separate in II; mitosis preserves starting ploidy.

beats.say: Growth और cell replacement में बार-बार mitosis चाहिए; meiosis खास reproductive stages से जुड़ा है। Germ-line cells भी mitosis कर सकती हैं। Land plants में meiosis सीधे gametes नहीं, spores बनाता है; उनसे बने gametophytes mitosis से gametes बनाते हैं।

frame.process: Identify meristematic cells in plant growing regions.
frame.how: Move from tissue location to cell outlines and internal vacuole description.
frame.when: Establish cell structure before explaining division and growth.
frame.conditions: The book's absent-vacuole description is an introductory simplification.
frame.atmosphere: A plant growing region enlarged to show its cells.

frame.process: Explain compact packing.
frame.how: Absent intercellular spaces mean neighbouring cells lie closely together.
frame.when: After individual cell features, examine neighbouring cells.
frame.conditions: Spaces between cells must be distinguished from compartments inside cells.
frame.atmosphere: A close view of adjacent meristematic cells.

frame.process: Connect cell division with production of new cells for growth.
frame.how: Preparation and division supply cells that can subsequently enlarge.
frame.when: During activity of a growing meristem; enlargement follows cell production.
frame.conditions: Division requires cellular preparation; 'only' describes the principal role, not absence of metabolism.
frame.atmosphere: An active plant growing region.

frame.process: Interpret the description 'highly active cells'.
frame.how: Connect the stated activity with the preceding cell-division statement.
frame.when: After explaining division.
frame.conditions: No numerical activity rate or formula is supplied.
frame.atmosphere: The two related textbook bullets shown together.

frame.process: Locate three meristems and connect position with growth.
frame.how: Trace the shoot from its tip through leaf bases to its side, then include root tips.
frame.when: Position is established before comparing length and girth effects.
frame.conditions: Apical includes both root and shoot tips; intercalary growth wording requires a node–internode distinction.
frame.atmosphere: An upright leafy shoot with highlighted growing regions.

frame.process: Read whole-plant and enlarged-shoot diagrams.
frame.how: Follow labels and insets in order, distinguishing growth arrows from identification callouts.
frame.when: After learning the locations and functions.
frame.conditions: The orientation of a tissue mark does not itself establish growth direction.
frame.atmosphere: A whole plant with coloured arrows beside an enlarged leafy shoot.

frame.process: Compare proposed locations with the taught locations.
frame.how: Check each statement against location and growth criteria.
frame.when: After diagram reading and before selecting an option.
frame.conditions: The restriction 'only' must be evaluated as part of statement 1.
frame.atmosphere: A three-row meristem-location question.

frame.process: Select the correct combination of statements.
frame.how: Reject statement 1 and retain statements 2 and 3.
frame.when: After checking all three statements.

beats.say: Plant की लंबाई और stem की मोटाई क्या एक ही जगह से बढ़ती हैं? आज position को growth से जोड़ेंगे।

videos.title: Permanent tissues: storage, flexibility और strength

frame.process: Permanent tissue cells take specialised roles rather than continuing meristematic division.
frame.how: Connect the stated loss of dividing ability with protection, support, storage and photosynthesis.
frame.when: After the preceding lesson on meristems and before differentiation is unpacked.
frame.conditions: Functions belong to different specialised cells, not necessarily every cell.
frame.atmosphere: Compare soft plant tissue, a bending stalk and coconut husk.

frame.process: Explain why the tissue is termed permanent.
frame.how: Trace changed dividing behaviour to a specialised role and the category name.
frame.when: After the permanent-tissue facts.
frame.conditions: Permanent does not mean immortal or incapable of any later change.
frame.atmosphere: A mature specialised region contrasted with an actively dividing meristem.

frame.process: Differentiation establishes specialised shape, size and function.
frame.how: Follow meristem-derived cells towards a mature specialised state.
frame.when: Following cell production; no fixed duration or separate biochemical stages are supplied.
frame.conditions: Do not confuse increased cell number with specialisation.
frame.atmosphere: A developing plant cell acquiring a particular job.

frame.process: Locate the wall and central vacuole in a mature plant cell.
frame.how: Read outside to inside and connect each structure with its contribution.
frame.when: Before comparing particular permanent tissues.
frame.conditions: Thick walls and large vacuoles are not universal across permanent tissues.
frame.atmosphere: A cutaway living mature plant cell.

frame.process: Define simple permanent tissue, chlorenchyma and aerenchyma.
frame.how: Move from examples to defining features, boundary tests and later use.
frame.when: Before the detailed parenchyma description.
frame.conditions: Chlorophyll and conspicuous air spaces identify different specialisations.
frame.atmosphere: Storage tissue, green tissue and floating aquatic plant parts.

frame.process: Establish parenchyma locations and storage or photosynthetic functions.
frame.how: Connect the introductory function statement with the detailed parenchyma bullets.
frame.when: After the definitions.
frame.conditions: Photosynthesis requires suitable chlorophyll-containing cells.
frame.atmosphere: Stem, root, leaf, flower and fruit.

frame.process: Place parenchyma first in the simple permanent tissue tree.
frame.how: Use wall structure, spaces and functional examples to distinguish branches.
frame.when: Before zooming into parenchyma cells.
frame.conditions: Specialised parenchyma remains within the parenchyma branch.
frame.atmosphere: A three-branch tissue classification.

frame.process: Describe parenchyma cell structure and arrangement.
frame.how: Inspect shape, thin wall and gaps between neighbouring cells.
frame.when: Immediately before reading its figure.
frame.conditions: Intercellular spaces are outside individual cell interiors.
frame.atmosphere: A cluster of loosely arranged living cells.

frame.process: Read the parenchyma figure and section key.
frame.how: Follow caption, a lengthwise, b cross section and the gap pointer.
frame.when: After the structural description.
frame.conditions: Correct the intended meaning of the printed intracellular label.
frame.atmosphere: Two complementary static views, not a process diagram.

frame.process: Read the paired collenchyma views.
frame.how: Follow a along elongated cells, then b across labelled cell walls.
frame.when: As the visual introduction to collenchyma.
frame.conditions: Identify both elongation and corner thickening.
frame.atmosphere: The middle tissue panel beside parenchyma.

frame.process: Place collenchyma second in the simple permanent tissue tree.
frame.how: Distinguish flexible support from storage and buoyancy.
frame.when: After the introductory figure.
frame.conditions: Photosynthesis is not an exclusive identifying feature.
frame.atmosphere: A leaf stalk contrasted with soft storage tissue.

frame.process: Establish collenchyma locations and stated functions.
frame.how: Connect dicot stems and leaf stalks with strength, flexibility and conditional photosynthesis.
frame.when: Before examining its wall arrangement.
frame.conditions: Photosynthesis requires suitable chloroplast-containing cells.
frame.atmosphere: Supported plant parts that can bend.

frame.process: Describe living elongated collenchyma cells.
frame.how: Read corner-thickened walls, close packing and living contents.
frame.when: Before the bending explanation.
frame.conditions: Retain the text's very little intercellular space wording.
frame.atmosphere: A close-up through a flexible supporting tissue.

frame.process: Explain flexible support and resulting bending.
frame.how: Link reinforced flexible walls to supported movement, with tendril and climber examples.
frame.when: When a plant part experiences a bending force.
frame.conditions: Flexible support differs from rigid reinforcement.
frame.atmosphere: Tendrils and climber stems bending around support.

frame.process: Read sclerenchyma fiber and stone-cell forms.
frame.how: Follow a fiber, b stone cell, shared lignin-wall label and internal lumen.
frame.when: Before the sclerenchyma text.
frame.conditions: Do not impose the shared section key on two explicitly named cell forms.
frame.atmosphere: The right-hand tissue panel.

frame.process: Establish sclerenchyma occurrence and protective support.
frame.how: Connect vascular surroundings, leaf veins and hard coverings with coconut husk.
frame.when: After the two cell forms are recognised.
frame.conditions: Recall husk as the precise coconut part named.
frame.atmosphere: Reinforced stems, veins and tough outer coverings.

frame.process: Describe mature sclerenchyma structure.
frame.how: Inspect lignified walls, absent intercellular spaces and lost living contents.
frame.when: At functional maturity.
frame.conditions: Long narrow shape primarily describes fibres, not every sclereid.
frame.atmosphere: A thick-walled supporting cell viewed outside to inside.

frame.process: Explain reduction of the cell cavity by wall thickening.
frame.how: Trace inward wall deposition to a progressively narrower lumen.
frame.when: During wall thickening.
frame.conditions: The book's absent-cavity statement is not universal; a narrow lumen can remain.
frame.atmosphere: A thick wall enclosing a very small internal space.

frame.process: Compare all three simple permanent tissues on eight criteria.
frame.how: Read each criterion across all tissues, then relate differences to function.
frame.when: After the individual tissues have been taught.
frame.conditions: Qualify the table's simplified spacing and occurrence statements.
frame.atmosphere: A three-column comparison table.

frame.process: Read the three comparative wall drawings.
frame.how: Move left to right through thin primary, irregularly thickened primary and thick secondary walls.
frame.when: After the comparison table.
frame.conditions: Use wall labels rather than schematic colour as identification evidence.
frame.atmosphere: Three adjacent static tissue drawings.

frame.process: Evaluate three tissue-feature statements.
frame.how: Compare each pairing with the taught reference features.
frame.when: Before selecting an answer option.
frame.conditions: The climber statement is imprecise and cannot exclude sclerenchyma from whole plants.
frame.atmosphere: A statement-based examination question.

frame.process: Select the intended answer to the statement question.
frame.how: Accept statement 1, reject statement 3 and qualify statement 2.
frame.when: After evaluating all three pairings.
frame.conditions: Distinguish intended examination association from an absolute biological rule.
frame.atmosphere: Choose among 1 only, 2 only, 1 and 3 only, and all incorrect.

frame.process: Identify the simple tissue with lignified walls.
frame.how: Match lignified secondary walls to sclerenchyma.
frame.when: After wall comparison.
frame.conditions: Answer within the supplied simple-tissue options.
frame.atmosphere: A direct multiple-choice question.

frame.process: Identify buoyant specialised parenchyma.
frame.how: Connect aquatic air spaces with aerenchyma and eliminate unrelated options.
frame.when: After parenchyma specialisations.
frame.conditions: Buoyancy depends on tissue arrangement, not just one isolated cell.
frame.atmosphere: An aquatic-plant multiple-choice question.

videos.title: Xylem और phloem: transport के अलग काम

frame.process: A complex permanent tissue contains several cell types.
frame.how: Read each tissue as an organised whole, then distinguish its component cells.
frame.when: Introduce the composition before individual transport roles.
frame.conditions: Complex refers to different cell types, not simply many cells.
frame.atmosphere: Picture the paired xylem and phloem anatomical drawings.

frame.process: Different cells coordinate in transport-related work.
frame.how: Conduction, storage and support contribute to a common tissue function.
frame.when: Establish the shared work before separating the two tissues.
frame.conditions: Transported materials include water, minerals and food.
frame.atmosphere: A plant needs connected transport pathways and supporting tissue.

frame.process: Complex permanent tissues are classified as xylem and phloem.
frame.how: Separate the branches by their principal transported materials.
frame.when: Classify before studying components.
frame.conditions: Both branches contain different cell types.
frame.atmosphere: A two-branch tissue classification.

frame.process: Xylem combines conducting cells, parenchyma and fibres.
frame.how: Move from the whole drawing to conducting elements, adjacent parenchyma and fibres.
frame.when: Describe mature conducting elements when discussing thick walls and dead contents.
frame.conditions: Do not extend the dead-cell description to living xylem parenchyma.
frame.atmosphere: A magnified xylem tissue group.

frame.process: Tubular tracheids and vessels provide vertical water-and-mineral pathways.
frame.how: Their elongated organisation provides an axial route.
frame.when: During conduction along the plant axis.
frame.conditions: A pathway is necessary; tubular shape alone is not the driving force.
frame.atmosphere: Contrast lengthwise conduction with sideways movement.

frame.process: Xylem parenchyma stores food and helps sideways conduction; fibres mainly support.
frame.how: Distinguish storage, lateral movement and mechanical reinforcement.
frame.when: These roles operate alongside axial conduction.
frame.conditions: Storage does not make xylem the main food-distribution tissue.
frame.atmosphere: Conducting cells surrounded by complementary components.

frame.process: Phloem includes five listed cell types, with fibres as the living-cell exception.
frame.how: Classify components by identity and then distinguish living elements from mature fibres.
frame.when: Discuss cell vitality at maturity.
frame.conditions: The five-type list spans plant groups; it is not a universal inventory for every plant.
frame.atmosphere: A phloem component tree with a marked fibre exception.

frame.process: Sieve-tube elements form a perforated conducting pathway.
frame.how: Read the tube, end sieve plates and adjoining elements.
frame.when: Food-containing sap passes between successive elements.
frame.conditions: Perforations allow continuity through the end partitions.
frame.atmosphere: An enlarged phloem conducting tube.

frame.process: Phloem carries food from leaves to other plant parts.
frame.how: Connect food-producing leaves with consuming or storing regions.
frame.when: Food moves according to source and sink locations.
frame.conditions: The leaf-to-other-parts example does not imply universally downward flow.
frame.atmosphere: A leaf supplying growing plant regions.

frame.process: Figures connect component anatomy to tissue position and illustrated transport.
frame.how: Read upper paired drawings, lower cellular enlargements, then the plant-axis overview.
frame.when: Identify structures before interpreting transport arrows.
frame.conditions: Leader lines name structures; the red arrow enlarges a region; black arrows depict flow.
frame.atmosphere: Successive magnifications from a plant axis to conducting cells.

frame.process: Compare transport, vitality, walls, permeability, wall materials and support.
frame.how: Read both sides criterion by criterion, then qualify broad table statements.
frame.when: After components and their functions have been established.
frame.conditions: Distinguish conducting elements from all cells in a complex tissue.
frame.atmosphere: A six-row comparison table with visible exception notes.

frame.process: Identify the option excluded from xylem.
frame.how: Assign each option to its tissue and interpret parenchyma in context.
frame.when: After learning component identities and exceptions.
frame.conditions: The question asks for the exception, not a conducting component.
frame.atmosphere: A four-option exam question.

videos.title: Plant की covering: protection और gas exchange

frame.process: Epidermis protects the primary plant body; its aerial cuticle restricts surface water loss.
frame.how: Explain the exposed covering and water-resistant cuticle, then distinguish the four options.
frame.when: Teach the protective relationship before answering the first question.
frame.conditions: Cuticle and epidermal thickness vary; 'thickest' is not a reliable general property.
frame.atmosphere: Picture a leaf or young stem exposed to surrounding air.

frame.process: Stomatal pores permit leaf gas exchange, while guard cells regulate their opening.
frame.how: Connect outside air to internal leaf spaces through pores and distinguish passage, controller and internal tissues.
frame.when: Explain exchange before solving the second question; opening permits both gas movement and water-vapour loss.
frame.conditions: Diffusion depends on concentration differences; guard-cell turgor alters pore opening.
frame.atmosphere: Picture the leaf epidermis separating internal air spaces from the atmosphere.

beats.say: Guard cells pore के आसपास की specialised epidermal cells हैं। उनके turgor, यानी पानी के कारण अंदर के pressure में बदलाव, pore का खुलना बदलते हैं। इसलिए वे gas movement और transpiration को regulate करती हैं: passage stomatal pore है, controller guard cells हैं।
